m v = 2 m V f ⟹ V f = v 2
Energy lost ∆ k 1 = 1 2 × m 2 2 m v 2 = 1 4 m v 2
For the collision between A + B and C.

∆ K = ∆ k 1 + ∆ k 2 = 1 4 m v 2 ( 1 + M 2 m + M )
⟹ ∆ K = 1 2 m v 2 × m + M 2 m + M = 5 6 ( 1 2 m v 2 )
⟹ m + M 2 m + M = 5 6 ⟹ 6 m + 6 M = 10 m + 5 M
⟹ M m = 4

Position vector of centre of mass of the system
              r C M = m 1 r 1 + m 2 r 2 m + m 2 = m 2 l j ^ + 2 m l j ^ m + 2 m = 4 m l j ^ 3 m = 4 l j ^ 3

question_text: The compound/s which will show significant intermolecular H–bonding is/are
solution_html:
Detailed Answer:


In o-nitrophenol intramolecular hydrogen bonding takes place.

Extensive H-bonding is observed in this case as two H-atoms bonded to strongly electronegative atoms (nitrogen, oxygen) are present. H-bonding occurs when H-bonded to strongly electronegative atoms exists in the vicinity of other electronegative atoms possessing lone pairs of electron.

Here, only one hydrogen atom bonded to electronegative oxygen atom is present. So, intermolecular H-bonding is present but not so extensive.  
So, option (a) is correct.

Consider the statements.
I. Bond length in N 2 + is 0.02Å greater than in N 2 .  
II. Bond length in N O + is 0.09 Å less than in NO.  
III. O 2 2 - has shorter bond length than O 2 .  
Which of the following statements are true?
question_text: Consider the statements. I. Bond length in N 2 + is 0.02Å greater than in N 2 . II. Bond length in N O + is 0.09 Å less than in NO. III. O 2 2 - has shorter bond length than O 2 . Which of the following statements are true?
solution_html:
Detailed Answer: Bond length is found to be inversely proportional to bond order. Greater the bond order, shorter is the bond length.  
I. Bond order of N 2 +   is 2.5 and that of N 2 is 3.  Thus, former bond is weaker and longer.  
II. Bond order of NO and N O + are 2.5 and 3 respectively. Thus, bond length of N O + is  less than NO.  
III. Bond order of O 2 2 - and O 2 are 1 and 2 respectively. Thus, O 2 2 - has longer bond length than O 2 .  
Thus, the correct statements are I and II.
solution_text: Detailed Answer: Bond length is found to be inversely proportional to bond order. Greater the bond order, shorter is the bond length. I. Bond order of N 2 + is 2.5 and that of N 2 is 3.  Thus, former bond is weaker and longer. II. Bond order of NO and N O + are 2.5 and 3 respectively. Thus, bond length of N O + is  less than NO. III. Bond order of O 2 2 - and O 2 are 1 and 2 respectively. Thus, O 2 2 - has longer bond length than O 2 . Thus, the correct statements are I and II.

question_text: Under which of the following specific conditions is the heat exchange of a chemical reaction ( q p ) identically equal to its change in internal energy ( Δ U ) for reactions involving real substances or gases?

options.html: 1 ) When the reaction is carried out in an open vessel at constant atmospheric pressure.
options.text: 1 ) When the reaction is carried out in an open vessel at constant atmospheric pressure.

options.html: 2 ) When the number of moles of gaseous products is exactly equal to the number of moles of gaseous reactants (<math> <mi>Δ</mi> <msub> <mrow> <mi>n</mi> </mrow> <mrow> <mi>g</mi> </mrow> </msub> </math>= 0).
options.text: 2 ) When the number of moles of gaseous products is exactly equal to the number of moles of gaseous reactants ( Δ n g = 0).

options.html: 3 ) When the reaction is strictly adiabatic.
options.text: 3 ) When the reaction is strictly adiabatic.

options.html: 4 ) When the system is isolated completely from the surroundings.
options.text: 4 ) When the system is isolated completely from the surroundings.

solution_html:
Detailed Answer: Enthalpy and internal energy are linked via the fundamental formula Δ H   =   Δ U   +   Δ ( P V ) . For chemical reactions involving gases, this maps to Δ H   =   Δ U   +   Δ n g R T . At constant pressure, the heat exchanged equals the enthalpy change ( q p   =   Δ H ). Therefore, q p   =   Δ U   +   Δ n g R T . When the net change in gaseous stoichiometric coefficients is zero ( Δ n g   =   0 ), the final pressure-volume work term drops out completely, making q p   =   Δ U .
Option D describes a scenario where heat transfer is prevented entirely, rather than a scenario where measurable reaction heat matches the system's total internal energy change.

solution_html:
Detailed Answer: For a real gas, intermolecular forces are present ( ∂ U ∂ V T ≠ 0 ). When a real gas expands at constant pressure, it must do extra work against these internal attractive forces alongside expanding against the external atmosphere. This demands an additional consumption of heat energy, causing C p - C v to deviate from exactly equalling R .
C p is always strictly greater than C v because constant volume heating does no boundary expansion work ( w = 0 ), meaning all heat goes directly into temperature rise, whereas constant pressure heating requires extra energy for expansion work.

solution_html:
Detailed Answer: Extensive properties depend directly on the total quantity or mass of matter present in the system. If you double the system size, these properties double. Examples include total mass ( M ), total volume ( V ), and internal energy ( U ).
Intensive properties are independent of the system size or the quantity of matter present. Examples include pressure ( P ), temperature ( T ), and density ( ρ ). (Note that density is the ratio of two extensive properties, mass / volume , which always yields an intensive property).

question_text: In a bomb calorimeter experiment used to measure the heat exchange of a combustion reaction, what physical property is kept strictly constant during the measurement process?
solution_html: Detailed Answer: A bomb calorimeter consists of a rigid, sealed steel vessel submerged in a water bath. Because the steel boundaries cannot flex or deform, the total volume of the reaction chamber remains completely fixed and constant (ΔV = 0). Consequently, no pressure-volume work can be done, so heat exchanged corresponds to the internal energy change (qv = ΔU).

question_html: A highly insulated system absorbs 1250 J of thermal energy from its surroundings while expanding against a constant external pressure of 1.5 bar. If the change in the volume of the container during this expansion is exactly 4.0 L, find the absolute change in the internal energy (ΔU) of the system in Joules. (Take 1 L-bar = 100 J)
question_text: A highly insulated system absorbs 1250 J of thermal energy from its surroundings while expanding against a constant external pressure of 1.5 bar. If the change in the volume of the container during this expansion is exactly 4.0 L, find the absolute change in the internal energy (ΔU) of the system in Joules. (Take 1 L-bar = 100 J)
solution_html:
Detailed Answer: Apply the First Law of Thermodynamics:
Δ U   =   q   +   w .
Heat is absorbed by the system, so q   =   + 1250   J .
The system expands against a constant external pressure, so the work done is:
w   =   - P e x t × Δ V = - ( 1.5   b a r ) × ( 4.0   L ) = - 6.0   L   b a r .
Convert work to Joules: w   =   - 6.0 × 100   J = - 600   J .
Substitute into first law: Δ U   =   1250   J   +   ( - 600   J ) = 650   J .
solution_text: Detailed Answer: Apply the First Law of Thermodynamics: Δ U = q + w . Heat is absorbed by the system, so q = + 1250 J . The system expands against a constant external pressure, so the work done is: w = - P e x t × Δ V = - ( 1.5 b a r ) × ( 4.0 L ) = - 6.0 L b a r . Convert work to Joules: w = - 6.0 × 100 J = - 600 J . Substitute into first law: Δ U = 1250 J + ( - 600 J ) = 650 J .

question_text: Two separate glass flasks, one containing 2.5 moles of an ideal gas at 400 K and the other completely evacuated, are connected by a stopcock valve inside an insulated container. When the valve is opened, the gas expands into the vacuum. Find the net final temperature of the combined flask system in Kelvin.
solution_html: Detailed Answer: Expansion into a vacuum (free expansion) means P e x t = 0, so work done w   =   0 . Since the flasks are placed inside an insulated container, the process is adiabatic, so q = 0. According to the First Law, Δ U   =   q   +   w = 0 + 0 = 0. For an ideal gas, internal energy depends only on temperature, so Δ U   =   0 implies that the temperature remains completely constant. Final temperature = 400   K .

question_text: The number of all five digit number which are divisible by 4 that can be formed from the digits 0, 1, 2, 3, 4 (without repetition) is -
solution_html:
Detailed Answer: The number formed will be divisible by 4 if the number formed by the two digits on the extreme right is divisible by 4, i.e. it should be 04, 12, 20, 24, 32, 40.
The number of numbers ending in 04 = 3! = 6
The number of numbers ending in 12 = 3! – 2! = 4
The number of numbers ending in 20 = 3! = 6
The number of numbers ending in 24 = 3! – 2! = 4
The number of numbers ending in 32 = 3! – 2! = 4
The number of numbers ending in 40 = 3! = 6
So, the required number = 6 + 4 + 6 + 4 + 4 + 6 = 30.

solution_html:
Detailed Answer: First vertex can be selected in 10C1 ways.

Now, two neighbouring vertices are not to be selected.
Among the remaining 7 vertices 3 are to be selected and 4 are not to be selected.
Now mark the 4 vertices not to be selected by × sign and then these can be partitioned by 5 partitions from these partitions we are to select 3. This can be done in 5C3 ways and these are the places where the remaining 3 vertices can be chosen.
number of ways = 10 C 1 × 5 C 3 4 = 25

⇒ K f = 20 3   J

question_text: A uniform bar of mass M and length L is horizontally suspended from the ceiling by two vertical light cables as shown. Cable A is connected 1/4th distance from the left end of the bar. Cable B is attached at the far right end of the bar. What is the tension in cable A?
solution_html:
Detailed Answer: This is a torque problem. While the fulcrum can be placed anywhere, placing it at the far right end of the bar eliminated cable B from the calculation. There are now only two forces acting on the bar; the weight that produces a counter clockwise rotation and the tension in cable A that produces a clockwise rotation. Since the bar is in equilibrium, these two torques must sum to zero.

Σ τ = T A ( 3 / 4   L ) - M g ⁡ ( 1 / 2   L ) = 0
Therefore    T A = ( M g L / 2 ) / ( 3   L / 4 ) = ( M g L / 2 ) ( 4 / 3   L ) = 2 M g / 3

Assertion: Hess's law can be used to calculate the enthalpy change of a reaction that cannot be measured experimentally.
Reason: Enthalpy ( H ) is a state function, meaning its change depends only on the initial and final states of the chemical system, not on the path taken.
In the light of the above statements choose the correct answer.
question_text: Below given are two statements. Assertion: Hess's law can be used to calculate the enthalpy change of a reaction that cannot be measured experimentally. Reason: Enthalpy ( H ) is a state function, meaning its change depends only on the initial and final states of the chemical system, not on the path taken. In the light of the above statements choose the correct answer.

options.html: 1 ) Assertion is correct statement but the reason is the wrong statement.
options.text: 1 ) Assertion is correct statement but the reason is the wrong statement.

options.html: 2 ) Both assertion and reasons are correct statements but the reason is not the correct explanation of the assertion.
options.text: 2 ) Both assertion and reasons are correct statements but the reason is not the correct explanation of the assertion.

options.html: 3 ) Assertion is wrong statement but the reason is the correct statement.
options.text: 3 ) Assertion is wrong statement but the reason is the correct statement.

options.html: 4 ) Both assertion and reasons are correct statements and the reason is the correct explanation of the assertion.
options.text: 4 ) Both assertion and reasons are correct statements and the reason is the correct explanation of the assertion.

solution_html: Detailed Answer: Hess's Law states that the total enthalpy change for a reaction is identical whether it occurs in one step or via multiple steps. This directly arises because enthalpy is a state function. This property enables us to calculate enthalpies for complex or dangerous slow processes (like tracking the formation of CO gas from graphite) using indirect known paths.

solution_html:
Detailed Answer: The reaction for formation of 1 mole of HCl is:
1 2   H 2 ( g ) + 1 2   C l 2 ( g ) → H C l ( g )
Δ r H ° = Σ Δ b o n d H ( r e a c t a n t s ) -   Σ Δ b o n d H ( p r o d u c t s )
Δ r H ° = [ 1 2   ×   Δ H ( H - H ) + 1 2   × Δ H ( C l - C l ) ] - [ 1 × Δ H ( H - C l ) ]
Δ r H ° = [ 1 2 × 434 + 1 2 × 242 ] - 431
  = [ 217 + 121 ] - 431 = 338 - 431 = - 93   k J / m o l .

The standard reaction enthalpy is Δ r H ° = + 60.0 k J / m o l and the standard reaction entropy is Δ r S ° = + 200 J / ( m o l · K ) . Assuming these values remain constant with temperature, determine the temperature threshold above which the reaction becomes thermodynamically spontaneous:
solution_html: Detailed Answer: To achieve a spontaneous forward reaction, we need Δ G   =   Δ H   -   T Δ S   <   0 . At the exact threshold of transition between non-spontaneous and spontaneous states, the system passes through equilibrium where Δ G   =   0 . Therefore, Δ H   =   T Δ S . Substituting the values (converting kJ to J): 60,000 J m o l =   T   200 J m o l · K = > T   = 60,000 200 = 300   K . Since Δ S is positive, increasing the temperature past 300 K makes the negative T Δ S term larger, resulting in Δ G   <   0 . Thus, T   >   300   K .

solution_html: Detailed Answer: For an endothermic reaction, ΔH is positive (+ve). For it to be spontaneous, ΔG = ΔH - TΔS must be negative (-ve). solution_html: Detailed Answer: The transition temperature (boiling point) is T = 100°C = 373 K. The condensation process is the direct reverse of vaporization, meaning Δ c o n d H °   =   - Δ v a p H ° = -40.66 kJ/mol = -40,660 J/mol. Since phase transitions are reversible at their equilibrium temperatures, Δ c o n d S ° = Δ c o n d H ° T   = -40,660 / 373 = -108.99 J/(mol·K). The sign must be negative because gas transforms into a more structured liquid.

solution_html: Detailed Answer: In an adiabatic free expansion into a vacuum, external pressure P e x t = 0 , so work w = 0 . Because it is adiabatic and insulated, heat q = 0. From the First Law, ΔU = q + w = 0, which means temperature remains constant (isothermal). Since the system is insulated, no heat is exchanged with the surroundings, so Δ S s u r r = 0 . solution_html: Detailed Answer: A rigid, highly insulated tank defines an isolated system because it cannot exchange matter (closed/rigid) or heat energy (insulated) with its outer surroundings. For any spontaneous process in an isolated system, the surroundings experience no change ( Δ S s u r r   =   0 ). Thus, according to the Second Law, Δ S u n i v = Δ S s y s + 0 > 0 , which means the system's own entropy change must be strictly greater than 0.

And 2 2010 = a 0 + a 1 ω 2 + a 2 ω + a 3 + a 4 ω 2 + … … ---(2)

A 60kg passenger goes from the earth to the mars in a spaceship moving with a constant velocity. Neglect all other objects in the sky. Which part of figure best represent the weight (Net gravitational force) of the passenger as a function of time
solution_html:
Detailed Answer: Weight of passenger on Earth =m×ge=60×10=600 N
Weight of passenger on Mars =m×gm=60×4=240 N
As the passenger is going from the Earth to the Mars in a spaceship moving with a constant velocity so the acceleration due to gravity because of Earth and Mars becomes negligible (zero) at some point in space.
Thus, weight of passenger becomes zero.
After sometime, as he reaches near to the Mars, his weight increases because of acceleration due to gravity of Mars.
Finally, at the surface of Mars, his weight becomes 240 N.

question_text: If b is the first term of an infinite G.P whose sum is five ,then b lies in the interval
solution_html:
Detailed Answer: Let b , b r , b r 2 , … … be an infinite G.P with first term b, common ratio r and sum =5
∴ 5 = b 1 - r ; | r | < 1   
⟹ b 5 = 1 - r ⟹ r = 1 - b 5   
Now, | r | < 1 ⟹ | 1 - b 5 | < 1 ⟹ - 1 < 1 - b 5 < 1    
⟹ 0 < - b 5 + 2 < 2     ⟹ 0 < 10 - b 5 < 2
⟹ 0 < - b + 10 < 10
⟹ - b + 10 > 0     a n d - b + 10 < 10
⟹ b < 10 and b > 0   or b ∈ ( 0,10 )
solution_text: Detailed Answer: Let b , b r , b r 2 , … … be an infinite G.P with first term b, common ratio r and sum =5 ∴ 5 = b 1 - r ; | r | < 1 ⟹ b 5 = 1 - r ⟹ r = 1 - b 5 Now, | r | < 1 ⟹ | 1 - b 5 | < 1 ⟹ - 1 < 1 - b 5 < 1 ⟹ 0 < - b 5 + 2 < 2 ⟹ 0 < 10 - b 5 < 2 ⟹ 0 < - b + 10 < 10 ⟹ - b + 10 > 0 a n d - b + 10 < 10 ⟹ b < 10 and b > 0 or b ∈ ( 0,10 )

question_text: Choose the correct statements from the following: 1. Steel is more elastic than rubber. 2. The stretching of a coil spring is determined by the Young’s modulus of the wire of the spring. 3. The frequency of a tuning fork is determined by the shear modulus of the material of the fork. 4. When a material is subjected to a tensile (stretching) stress the restoring forces are caused by interatomic attraction.
solution_html:
Detailed Answer: (a) Steel is more elastic than rubber.
Elasticity is measured by Young’s modulus.
Steel: Y ≈ 2 × 10 11   N/m 2
Rubber: Y ≈ 10 7 - 10 8   N/m 2
A larger Young’s modulus means less strain for the same stress, hence greater elasticity.
(b) The stretching of a coil spring is determined by the Young’s modulus of the wire of the spring.
When a helical spring is stretched, the wire mainly undergoes twisting (shearing) rather than direct stretching.
Therefore, the extension depends primarily on the shear modulus (modulus of rigidity), not Young’s modulus.
(c) The frequency of a tuning fork is determined by the shear modulus of the material of the fork.
The vibration frequency of a tuning fork depends on the elastic properties of the material. For transverse vibrations, the relevant elastic constant is the shear modulus (modulus of rigidity).
(d) When a material is subjected to a tensile (stretching) stress the restoring forces are caused by interatomic attraction.
Stretching increases the distance between atoms/molecules. The restoring force arises due to interatomic attractive forces trying to bring the atoms back to their equilibrium positions
solution_text: Detailed Answer: (a) Steel is more elastic than rubber. Elasticity is measured by Young’s modulus. Steel: Y ≈ 2 × 10 11 N/m 2 Rubber: Y ≈ 10 7 - 10 8 N/m 2 A larger Young’s modulus means less strain for the same stress, hence greater elasticity. (b) The stretching of a coil spring is determined by the Young’s modulus of the wire of the spring. When a helical spring is stretched, the wire mainly undergoes twisting (shearing) rather than direct stretching. Therefore, the extension depends primarily on the shear modulus (modulus of rigidity), not Young’s modulus. (c) The frequency of a tuning fork is determined by the shear modulus of the material of the fork. The vibration frequency of a tuning fork depends on the elastic properties of the material. For transverse vibrations, the relevant elastic constant is the shear modulus (modulus of rigidity). (d) When a material is subjected to a tensile (stretching) stress the restoring forces are caused by interatomic attraction. Stretching increases the distance between atoms/molecules. The restoring force arises due to interatomic attractive forces trying to bring the atoms back to their equilibrium positions

solution_html:
Detailed Answer: Assertion (A): When a rod lying freely is heated, no thermal stress is developed in it.
A freely placed rod is free to expand on heating, so no opposing force acts on it. Hence, no thermal stress develops.
Reason (R): On heating, the length of the rod increases.
The rod expands due to thermal expansion: Δ L = α L Δ T
Since the rod is free to increase its length, this expansion occurs without any constraint, and therefore no thermal stress is produced.
Hence, the reason correctly explains the assertion.

question_html: A block of mass m produces an extension of 9 cm in an elastic spring of length 60 cm when it is hung by it, and the system is in equilibrium. The spring is cut in two parts of 40 cm and 20 cm lengths. The same block hangs in equilibrium with the help of these two parts. Find the extension (in cm) in this case.
question_text: A block of mass m produces an extension of 9 cm in an elastic spring of length 60 cm when it is hung by it, and the system is in equilibrium. The spring is cut in two parts of 40 cm and 20 cm lengths. The same block hangs in equilibrium with the help of these two parts. Find the extension (in cm) in this case.
solution_html:
Detailed Answer: Step 1: Spring constants of the two pieces
Let the spring constant of the original spring be k .
For the 40 cm piece:
k 1 = k 60 40 = 3 k 2   
For the 20 cm piece:
k 2 = k 60 20 = 3 k
Step 2: Pieces used together
The two pieces support the same mass one below the other, so they act as springs in series.
1 k e q = 1 k 1 + 1 k 2
1 k e q = 2 3 k + 1 3 k = 1 k
Thus, k e q = k
Step 3: Extension with the same mass
Since the equivalent spring constant remains k , x ’ = m g k e q = m g k = 9  cm
solution_text: Detailed Answer: Step 1: Spring constants of the two pieces Let the spring constant of the original spring be k . For the 40 cm piece: k 1 = k 60 40 = 3 k 2 For the 20 cm piece: k 2 = k 60 20 = 3 k Step 2: Pieces used together The two pieces support the same mass one below the other, so they act as springs in series. 1 k e q = 1 k 1 + 1 k 2 1 k e q = 2 3 k + 1 3 k = 1 k Thus, k e q = k Step 3: Extension with the same mass Since the equivalent spring constant remains k , x ’ = m g k e q = m g k = 9 cm

The area of the bottom =     r 2   =   3.14     0.1   m 2
=   0.0314   m 2 .  
The force on the bottom is, therefore,
F   =   P     r 2
= ( 1.01     10 5   P a )   ( 0.0314   m 2 ) = 3230   N .

The pressure at the bottom is P = P 0 + h g = 1.01 10 5 P a + ( 0.20 m ) ( 1000 k g / m 3 ) ( 10 m / s 2 ) = 1.01 10 5 P a + 0.02 10 5 P a = 1.03 10 5 P a . The area of the bottom = r 2 = 3.14 0.1 m 2 = 0.0314 m 2 . The force on the bottom is, therefore, F = P r 2 = ( 1.01 10 5 P a )   ( 0.0314 m 2 ) = 3230 N .

Pressure equation from manometer

question_text: A uniform solid cylinder of density 0.8 g/cm 3 floats in equilibrium in a combination of two non-mixing liquids A and B with its axis vertical. The densities of the liquids A and B are 0.7 g/cm 3 and 1.2 g/cm 3 , respectively. The height of liquid A is h A = 1.2 cm. The length of the part of the cylinder immersed in liquid B is h B = 0.8 cm. The cylinder is depressed in such a way that its top surface is just below the upper surface of liquid A and is then released. The acceleration of the cylinder immediately after it is released is :
solution_html:
Detailed Answer: Let   ρ be the density and A be the area of cross section of the cylinder
Initially, net force on the cylinder is zero. Hence
σ A A h A g + σ B A h B g - ρ A ( h + h A + h B ) g = 0
⟹ 0.7 × 1.2 + 1.2 × 0.8 - 0.8 ( h + 2 ) = 0
⟹ h = 0.25 c m
Hence , the height of the cylinder is L = 2.25 cm
When the cylinder is immersed completely and then released , the equation of motion of the cylinder is :
σ A A h A g + σ B A ( h B + 0.25 ) g - ρ A L g = ρ A L a
( 0.7 × 1.2 + 1.2 × 1.05 - 0.8 × 2.25 ) g = ρ L a
⟹ 0.3 g ρ L = a ⟹ a = 0.3 g 0.8 × 2.25 = g 6
solution_text: Detailed Answer: Let ρ be the density and A be the area of cross section of the cylinder Initially, net force on the cylinder is zero. Hence σ A A h A g + σ B A h B g - ρ A ( h + h A + h B ) g = 0 ⟹ 0.7 × 1.2 + 1.2 × 0.8 - 0.8 ( h + 2 ) = 0 ⟹ h = 0.25 c m Hence , the height of the cylinder is L = 2.25 cm When the cylinder is immersed completely and then released , the equation of motion of the cylinder is : σ A A h A g + σ B A ( h B + 0.25 ) g - ρ A L g = ρ A L a ( 0.7 × 1.2 + 1.2 × 1.05 - 0.8 × 2.25 ) g = ρ L a ⟹ 0.3 g ρ L = a ⟹ a = 0.3 g 0.8 × 2.25 = g 6

Therefore, the entropy change for the dissolution of a gas is always negative (ΔS < 0).

solution_html: Detailed Answer: A highly positive deviation from Raoult's law means that the liquid molecules find it much easier to escape into the vapor phase compared to their pure states because the A-B interactions are weaker than A-A and B-B interactions. According to the direct relationship between vapor pressure and boiling point, a maximum in vapor pressure creates a corresponding sharp minimum in the boiling point curve. This is called a minimum boiling azeotrope. At this point, the liquid and vapor phases have identical compositions, causing the mixture to boil at a constant temperature without any change in composition.

Therefore, for solid solutes whose dissolution is endothermic, solubility increases consistently with rising temperatures.

solution_html: Detailed Answer: For any ideal solution (such as benzene + toluene), the intermolecular forces between the solute and solvent (A-B interactions) are exactly equal in magnitude to the cohesive forces within the pure components (A-A and B-B). Consequently, there is absolutely no contraction or expansion of volume upon mixing. Therefore, Δ V m i x i n g = 0 mL exactly.

question_text: For a binary liquid mixture showcasing a large positive deviation from Raoult's law, a maximum vapor pressure is achieved at a specific composition. At this composition, the solution boils at a constant minimum temperature. How many fractional components are obtained if this azeotropic mixture is subjected to standard fractional distillation?
solution_html: Detailed Answer: An azeotropic mixture behaves chemically like a single pure substance because its liquid phase composition is identical to its vapor phase composition (x = y). Therefore, when boiled, the entire mixture distills over at a constant temperature without any change in composition. It cannot be separated into individual components by fractional distillation, yielding just 1 continuous unseparated dynamic collection fraction.

question_text: A bottle of aqueous hydrofluoric acid (HF) is labeled as 24.5 M and has a density of 1.20 g/mL. Calculate the molality (m) of this solution divided by 5. (Molar mass of HF = 20 g/mol). Round off to the nearest integer.
solution_html:
Detailed Answer: Step-by-Step Derivation: Consider 1 Liter of this solution.
1. Mass of solution = 1000 mL × 1.20 g/mL = 1200 grams.
2. Moles of HF = 24.5 moles.
3. Mass of HF solute = 24.5 × 20 = 490 grams.
4. Mass of solvent water = 1200 g - 490 g = 710 grams = 0.710 kg.
5. Molality (m) = Moles / Mass of solvent (kg) = 24.5 / 0.710 = 34.5 m.
6. Dividing by 5: 34.5 / 5 = 6.9. Rounding off to the nearest integer gives 7.

question_html:
Which of the following statements regarding the mechanism of heat transfer by convection is incorrect?
A. Convection involves the actual bulk movement of the matter particles themselves to transfer heat energy from a high-temperature zone to a low-temperature zone.
B. Natural (or free) convection occurs entirely due to gravity and density differences within a fluid caused by thermal expansion.
C. Forced convection occurs when a fluid is compelled to move across a surface by external mechanical means such as a pump, fan, or blower.
D. Liquid water cannot experience natural convection when heated from the top surface because warm water is denser than cold water and will sink
question_text: Which of the following statements regarding the mechanism of heat transfer by convection is incorrect? A. Convection involves the actual bulk movement of the matter particles themselves to transfer heat energy from a high-temperature zone to a low-temperature zone. B. Natural (or free) convection occurs entirely due to gravity and density differences within a fluid caused by thermal expansion. C. Forced convection occurs when a fluid is compelled to move across a surface by external mechanical means such as a pump, fan, or blower. D. Liquid water cannot experience natural convection when heated from the top surface because warm water is denser than cold water and will sink
solution_html:
Detailed Answer: The incorrect statement is (d)
Warm water is actually less dense than cold water (except in the anomalous range below 4 ℃ . If you heat water from the top, the warmer, lighter water stays at the top surface, and the colder, heavier water stays at the bottom. Because of this, gravity-driven density loops cannot form, and natural convection fails to establish (heat travels down mostly via slow conduction instead). The statement incorrectly claims that warm water is denser and will sink.

question_html: Which of the following statements about the freezing process of an aqueous solution of sucrose is CORRECT?
question_text: Which of the following statements about the freezing process of an aqueous solution of sucrose is CORRECT?

options.html: 1 ) As the solution is cooled below its freezing point, sucrose crystals separate out first.
options.text: 1 ) As the solution is cooled below its freezing point, sucrose crystals separate out first.

options.html: 2 ) The vapor pressure of the solution becomes equal to the vapor pressure of the pure solid solute at the freezing point.
options.text: 2 ) The vapor pressure of the solution becomes equal to the vapor pressure of the pure solid solute at the freezing point.

options.html: 3 ) The concentration of sucrose in the remaining liquid phase increases as freezing progresses, causing the freezing point to drop further.
options.text: 3 ) The concentration of sucrose in the remaining liquid phase increases as freezing progresses, causing the freezing point to drop further.

options.html: 4 ) Freezing point depression constant (<math> <msub> <mrow> <mi>K</mi> </mrow> <mrow> <mi>f</mi> </mrow> </msub> </math>) changes value dynamically as the solute concentration changes.
options.text: 4 ) Freezing point depression constant ( K f ) changes value dynamically as the solute concentration changes.

solution_html: Detailed Answer: When an aqueous solution freezes, the pure solvent (ice) separates out first. As pure water freezes out, the remaining liquid solution becomes increasingly concentrated with sucrose. According to Δ T f = K f ⋅ m , an increase in molality causes a further depression of the freezing point dynamically, making statement (c) correct. Statement (a) is false (solvent separates). Statement (b) is false (it equals the vapor pressure of the solid solvent). Statement (d) is false ( K f     is a solvent-specific constant).

question_text: A solution is prepared by dissolving 120 g of a non-volatile, non-electrolyte solute Y ( m o l a r m a s s = 60 g m o l ⁻ ¹ ) in 180 g of water at 300 K. If the vapour pressure of pure water at this temperature is 240 torr, calculate the lowering of vapour pressure ( Δ p ) i n t o r r .
solution_html:
Detailed Answer: Calculate the moles of solute (n₂):
n ₂   =   M a s s   /   M o l a r   M a s s   =   120   g   /   60   g   m o l ⁻ ¹   =   2   m o l e s .
Calculate the moles of solvent (n₁ - water):
n ₁   =   M a s s   /   M o l a r   M a s s   =   180   g   /   18   g   m o l ⁻ ¹   =   10   m o l e s .
Calculate the mole fraction of solute in the solution (χ₂):
Wait, the exact law of Relative Lowering of Vapour Pressure (Raoult’s Law) states:
  Δ p   /   p ⁰   =   ( p ⁰   -   p )   /   p ⁰   =   χ ₂   =   n ₂   /   ( n ₁   +   n ₂ )
  χ ₂   =   2   /   ( 10   +   2 )   =   2   /   12   =   1 / 6 .
C a l c u l a t e   t h e   l o w e r i n g   o f   v a p o u r   p r e s s u r e   ( Δ p ) : Δ p   =   p ⁰   ×   χ ₂   =   240   t o r r   ×   ( 1 / 6 )   =   40   t o r r .
solution_text: Detailed Answer: Calculate the moles of solute (n₂): n ₂ = M a s s / M o l a r M a s s = 120 g / 60 g m o l ⁻ ¹ = 2 m o l e s . Calculate the moles of solvent (n₁ - water): n ₁ = M a s s / M o l a r M a s s = 180 g / 18 g m o l ⁻ ¹ = 10 m o l e s . Calculate the mole fraction of solute in the solution (χ₂): Wait, the exact law of Relative Lowering of Vapour Pressure (Raoult’s Law) states: Δ p / p ⁰ = ( p ⁰ - p ) / p ⁰ = χ ₂ = n ₂ / ( n ₁ + n ₂ ) χ ₂ = 2 / ( 10 + 2 ) = 2 / 12 = 1 / 6 . C a l c u l a t e t h e l o w e r i n g o f v a p o u r p r e s s u r e ( Δ p ) : Δ p = p ⁰ × χ ₂ = 240 t o r r × ( 1 / 6 ) = 40 t o r r .

question_text: The number of points with integral coordinates that are interior to the circle x 2 + y 2 = 16 is
solution_html:
Detailed Answer: The number of points is equal to the number of integral solutions (x, y) such that
x 2 + y 2 < 16 .
So, x, y are integers such that - 3 ≤ x ≤ 3 , - 3 ≤ y ≤ 3 satisfying the inequation x 2 + y 2 < 16 .
The number of selections of values of x is 7, namely –3, –2, –1, 0, 1, 2, 3.
The same is true for y. So the number of ordered pairs (x, y) is 7×7.
But (3, 3), (3, –3), (–3, 3), (–3, –3) are rejected because they do not satisfy the inequation
x 2 + y 2 < 16 .
So the number of points is 45.

B. First law of thermodynamics gives concept of internal energy

question_text: Consider the following statements: A. Zeroth law of thermodynamics gives concept of temperature B. First law of thermodynamics gives concept of internal energy C. In isothermal expansion of ideal gas, ∆ Q ≠ ∆ W D. Product of intensive and extensive variables is extensive E. The ratio of any extensive variable to mass will be an extensive variable. Choose the correct combination of statements from the options given below:
solution_html:
Detailed Answer: The Zeroth Law states that if two systems are each in thermal equilibrium with a third system, they are in thermal equilibrium with each other, i.e., the Zeroth law gives idea about the property of temperature to be measured. Hence, statement A is true.
The first law of thermodynamics
ΔQ = ΔU + ΔW
This relation introduces internal energy (ΔU) as a state function which is based on energy conservation. Hence, statement B is true.
In an isothermal expansion of an ideal gas, temperature remains constant, so, ΔU=0. Now from first law of thermodynamics,
ΔQ = ΔU + ΔW
ΔQ = 0 + ΔW ⟹ ∆ Q =   ∆ W
But as per statement C, in isothermal process
∆ Q ≠ ∆ W , So, statement C is False.
Intensive variables are the properties which do not depend on size, for example temperature and pressure.
Extensive variables are the properties depend on size, for example volume.
The product of intensive and extensive property ( P × V )   represents work or energy, which depends with the size of the system. Therefore, the product is extensive.
When an extensive variable (like volume or heat capacity) is divided by mass, it becomes a specific quantity (like specific volume or specific heat). Specific quantities are intensive because they do not depend on the total mass of the system. Statement E says it remains extensive, so it is False.
Therefore, only A, B, and D are correct. Hence, the correct option is (C).

Hence, statement B is true. In an isothermal expansion of an ideal gas, temperature remains constant, so, ΔU=0. Now from first law of thermodynamics, ΔQ = ΔU + ΔW ΔQ = 0 + ΔW ⟹ ∆ Q = ∆ W But as per statement C, in isothermal process ∆ Q ≠ ∆ W , So, statement C is False. The product of intensive and extensive property ( P × V ) represents work or energy, which depends with the size of the system. Therefore, the product is extensive. When an extensive variable (like volume or heat capacity) is divided by mass, it becomes a specific quantity (like specific volume or specific heat). Specific quantities are intensive because they do not depend on the total mass of the system. Statement E says it remains extensive, so it is False. Therefore, only A, B, and D are correct. Hence, the correct option is (C).

Detailed Answer: Given, P = a V - 3
The isothermal bulk modulus is defined as
K T = - V ( d P d V ) T
Differentiate P = a V - 3 with respect to V :
d P d V = - 3 a V - 4
Therefore, K T = - V ( - 3 a V - 4 ) = 3 a V - 3
Since P = a V - 3 , we get K T = 3 P Answer: (b) 3 P
solution_text: Detailed Answer: Given, P = a V - 3 The isothermal bulk modulus is defined as K T = - V ( d P d V ) T Differentiate P = a V - 3 with respect to V : d P d V = - 3 a V - 4 Therefore, K T = - V ( - 3 a V - 4 ) = 3 a V - 3 Since P = a V - 3 , we get K T = 3 P Answer: (b) 3 P

question_text: 5.6 litres of helium gas at STP is adiabatically compressed to 0.7 litre. Taking the initial temperature to be T 1 , the work done in the process is:
solution_html:
Detailed Answer: Given: Initial volume, V 1 = 5.6  L
Final volume, V 2 = 0.7  L , Helium is a monoatomic gas, so, γ = 5 3 compression is adiabatic.
First, find the compression ratio:
V 1 V 2 = 5.6 0.7 = 8
For an adiabatic process,
T 2 = T 1 ( V 1 V 2 ) γ - 1
= T 1 ( 8 ) 2 / 3 = T 1 ( 2 3 ) 2 / 3 = 4 T 1
Now, the work done on the gas is equal to the increase in internal energy:
W = Δ U = n C V ( T 2 - T 1 )
For helium,
C V = 3 R 2
The number of moles is
P V = N r t
n = 5.6 22.4 = 1 4
Hence,
W = 1 4 ⋅ 3 R 2   ( 4 T 1 - T 1 )
= 1 4 ⋅ 3 R 2 ⋅ 3 T 1
= 9 8 R T 1
Correct option: a. 9 8 R T 1

question_text: A gas expands with temperature according to the relation V = K T 2 3 . What is the work done when the temperature changes by 30 0 C ?
solution_html:
Detailed Answer: For 1 mole of gas, P = R T V .
Given: V = K T 2 3 .
Differentiate with respect to temperature, T:
d V = d V d T d T = 2 3 K T - 1 3 d T
Work done is W = ∫ P d V
Substituting P = R T V and the expression for dV:
W = ∫ P d V = ∫ ( R T V ) ( 2 3 K T - 1 3 d T )
W = ∫ P d V = ∫ ( R T K T 2 3 ) ( 2 3 K T - 1 3 d T )
W = 2 3 ∫ R T ( 1 - 2 3 - 1 3 ) d T = 2 3 ∫ R T 0 d T
W = 2 3 ∫ R d T = 2 3 ∫ R ∆ T
Substituting, ∆ T = 30 0 C , we get
W = 2 3 × R × 30 = 20   R
Option (b)
solution_text: Detailed Answer: For 1 mole of gas, P = R T V . Given: V = K T 2 3 . Differentiate with respect to temperature, T: d V = d V d T d T = 2 3 K T - 1 3 d T Work done is W = ∫ P d V Substituting P = R T V and the expression for dV: W = ∫ P d V = ∫ ( R T V ) ( 2 3 K T - 1 3 d T ) W = ∫ P d V = ∫ ( R T K T 2 3 ) ( 2 3 K T - 1 3 d T ) W = 2 3 ∫ R T ( 1 - 2 3 - 1 3 ) d T = 2 3 ∫ R T 0 d T W = 2 3 ∫ R d T = 2 3 ∫ R ∆ T Substituting, ∆ T = 30 0 C , we get W = 2 3 × R × 30 = 20 R Option (b)

Its initial thermodynamic state at pressure P i =10 5 Pa and volume V i = 10 -3 m 3 changes to a final state at P f = ( 1 32 ) × 10 5 P a and V f = 8 × 10 - 3 m 3 in an adiabatic quasi-static process, such that P 3 V 5 = c o n s t a n t . This can be rewritten in the standard form as:
P V 5 3 = c o n s t a n t . For this equation γ= 5 3 , which indicates monoatomic gas.

=   ( 1 32 ) × 10 5 × 8 × 10 - 3 - 10 5 × 10 - 3 5 3 - 1

W i s o b a r i c =   P i ( V f - V i )
W i s o b a r i c = 10 5 × ( 8 × 10 - 3 - 10 - 3 )
W i s o b a r i c = 10 5 ( 7 × 10 - 3 ) = 700   J
Step 2: work done during isochoric process:
Since the volume is constant Vf , the work done is zero.
W i s o c h o r i c = 0
Total work done,
Wtotal = W i s o b a r i c + W i s o c h o r i c =700 + 0 =700J
Using the First Law of Thermodynamics:
Q = ∆ U + W t o t a l = - 112.5 + 700 = 587.5   J
~ 588   J
Option (c)

An isobaric process involves constant pressure conditions ( ∆ P = 0 ), but internal energy ( ∆ U ) can change. Thus, it's associated with (III).

(B) Adiabatic → (II)

solution_html:
Detailed Answer: For an ideal gas,
P = ρ R s T
where ρ is the density and R s is the specific gas constant.
Hence, on a P - ρ diagram,
P ρ = R s T
So, straight lines passing through the origin represent constant-temperature (isothermal) lines, and a steeper line corresponds to a higher temperature.
From the diagram:
Points a and b lie on the lower isotherm T 1 .
Points c and d lie on the higher isotherm T 2 .
Therefore,
T c = T d > T a = T b
Checking the statements

Along b c , density remains constant ( ρ = ρ 1 ).
Since
ρ = m V ,
constant density implies constant volume.
Therefore,
W b c = ∫ P   d V = 0 .
True
(b) Work done by the gas in process c d is negative.
Along c d , density increases from ρ 1 to ρ 2 .
Since V = m ρ , volume decreases. Thus, the gas is compressed and d V < 0 . Hence, W c d = ∫ P   d V < 0 . True
(c) Internal energy of the gas at point a is greater than at state c .
For an ideal gas,
U ∝ T .
Since T c > T a , U c > U a . Therefore the statement is
❌ False
(d) Net work done by the gas in the cycle is negative.
The cycle is traversed as
a → b → c → d → a .
a b : compression ( W < 0 )
b c : W = 0
c d : compression ( W < 0 )
d a : constant density ( W = 0 )
Thus, the total work done by the gas is negative:
W cycle = W a b + W c d < 0 .
True

question_text: The correct order of equivalent conductance at infinite dilution of L i C l , N a C l and K C l is

2 ) K C l > N a C l > L i C l
3 ) N a C l > K C l > L i C l
4 ) L i C l > K C l > N a C l

solution_html:
Detailed Answer: At infinite dilution, equivalent conductance depends on ionic mobility.
Among alkali metals, K + > N a + > L i + in ionic mobility due to the decreasing degree of hydration.
Hence, K C l > N a C l > L i C l in equivalent conductance

solution_html: Detailed Answer: Solution which contains large number of ions compared to another solution of same concentration at the same temperature has more conductance and is said to be stronger electrolyte. If concentration of respective electrolyte is increased, the equivalent conductance decreases in each case, but rapid decrease in equivalent conductance is seen in weak electrolyte.

options.html: 3 ) Decrease in the self-ionization of water.

solution_html:
Detailed Answer: Molar conductivity ( Λ m ) increases on dilution because
As the solution is diluted, the distance between ions increases.
Interionic attractions decrease, allowing ions to move more freely under an electric field.
Greater ionic mobility leads to higher molar conductivity.
For HCl, which is a strong electrolyte, it is already almost completely ionized even at moderate concentrations.

solution_html:
Detailed Answer: We can solve this using the ideal gas law with the combined effect of temperature rise and volume expansion.
Step 1: Initial conditions
Initial pressure: P 1 = 200  kPa
Initial temperature: T 1 = 22 ∘ C = 295  K
Final temperature: T 2 = 42 ∘ C = 315  K
Volume expansion: V 2 = 1.02 V 1 (2% increase)
Step 2: Ideal gas relation
P 1 V 1 T 1 = P 2 V 2 T 2
Rearranging for P 2 :
P 2 = P 1 ⋅ T 2 T 1 ⋅ V 1 V 2
Step 3: Substitution
P 2 = 200 ⋅ 315 295 ⋅ 1 1.02
P 2 ≈ 200 ⋅ 1.0678 ⋅ 0.9804
P 2 ≈ 209.7  kPa

question_html: At what temperature does the average translational kinetic energy of a molecule in a gas equal to the kinetic energy of an electron accelerated from rest through a potential difference of 5 volt.
question_text: At what temperature does the average translational kinetic energy of a molecule in a gas equal to the kinetic energy of an electron accelerated from rest through a potential difference of 5 volt.
solution_html:
Detailed Answer: Average Translational Kinetic Energy of a Molecule (Km):
K m = 3 2 K B T
where,
KB is the Boltzmann constant (1.38×10-23 JK-1) and T is the absolute temperature.
Kinetic Energy of an Electron (Ke):
Ke=qV
where q is the elementary charge (1 . 6 × 10 - 19 )
and V is the potential difference (5Volt).
Solving for Temperature:
Set K m = K e
3 2 K B T = q V
T = 2 q V 3 K B
Substitute the values:
T = 2 × 1.6 × 10 - 19 × 5 3 × 1.38 × 10 - 23 = 16 × 10 - 19 4.14 × 10 - 23
T = 3.865 × 10 4 K
T = 38.65 × 10 3 K
solution_text: Detailed Answer: Average Translational Kinetic Energy of a Molecule (K m ): K m = 3 2 K B T where, K B is the Boltzmann constant (1.38×10 -23 JK -1 ) and T is the absolute temperature. Kinetic Energy of an Electron (K e ): K e =qV where q is the elementary charge (1 . 6 × 10 - 19 ) and V is the potential difference (5Volt). Solving for Temperature: Set K m = K e 3 2 K B T = q V T = 2 q V 3 K B Substitute the values: T = 2 × 1.6 × 10 - 19 × 5 3 × 1.38 × 10 - 23 = 16 × 10 - 19 4.14 × 10 - 23 T = 3.865 × 10 4 K T = 38.65 × 10 3 K

Engine B absorbs half of the heat rejected by engine A and rejects heat to the sink at T 3 . When work done in both the cases is equal, the value of T is:
solution_html:
Detailed Answer: To find the value of(T), we equate the work done by both Carnot engines based on the given conditions:
Work done by Engine A (WA):
Engine A operates between T1 and T. The relationship between heat absorbed Q1 and heat rejected Q2 is:
Q 1 T 1   = Q 2 T ⟹ Q 2 = Q 1 ( T T 1 )
The work done by Engine A is:
W A = Q 1 - Q 2 = Q 1 ( 1 - T T 1 )
Work done by Engine B (WB):
Engine B absorbs heat Q3, which is half of the heat rejected by A ( Q 3 = 1 2 Q 2 ), and operates between T and T3.
The work done by Engine B is:
W B = Q 3 ( 1 - T 3 T ) = 1 2 Q 2 ( 1 - T 3 T )  
Substitute, Q 2 = Q 1 ( T T 1 ) one gets,
W B = 1 2 Q 1 ( T T 1 ) ( 1 - T 3 T )
W B = 1 2 Q 1 ( T T 1 ) ( T - T 3 T ) = Q 1 ( T - T 3 ) 2 T 1
Equating work WA=WB:
Q 1 ( 1 - T T 1 ) =   Q 1 ( T - T 3 ) 2 T 1   
( T 1 - T T 1 ) = ( T - T 3 ) 2 T 1
2 ( T 1 - T ) = ( T - T 3 )
2 T 1 - 2 T = T - T 3
2 T 1 + T 3 = 3 T
T = 2 3 T 1 + 1 3 T 3
Option (a)

question_text: As shown in the figure, five Carnot engines, each having the same efficiency η and operating with the same number of cycles per unit time, work between six heat reservoirs. The heat rejected by one engine is completely absorbed by the next engine. Let Q 0 be the heat absorbed per cycle by the first engine and W be the total work done per cycle by all the engines together. If the overall efficiency of the system is η net = W Q 0 = 211 243 , then the efficiency η of each Carnot engine is:
solution_html:
Detailed Answer: Given
Number of Carnot engines = 5
Efficiency of each engine = η
Heat rejected by one engine is completely absorbed by the next.
Net efficiency of the combination:
η net = W Q 0 = 211 243
Step 1: Heat flow through the engines
Let the first engine absorb heat Q 0 .
For the first engine,
η = W 1 Q 0
Hence heat rejected by the first engine is
Q 1 = Q 0 - W 1 = Q 0 ( 1 - η )
Since Q 1 is absorbed by the second engine,
Q 2 = ( 1 - η ) Q 1 = ( 1 - η ) 2 Q 0
Similarly,
Q 3 = ( 1 - η ) 3 Q 0
Q 4 = ( 1 - η ) 4 Q 0
Q 5 = ( 1 - η ) 5 Q 0
Step 2: Total work done
Work done by each engine:
W 1 = Q 0 - Q 1
W 2 = Q 1 - Q 2
W 3 = Q 2 - Q 3
W 4 = Q 3 - Q 4
W 5 = Q 4 - Q 5
Adding all,
W = W 1 + W 2 + W 3 + W 4 + W 5  
W = ( Q 0 - Q 1 ) + ( Q 1 - Q 2 ) + ( Q 2 - Q 3 ) + ( Q 3 - Q 4 ) + ( Q 4 - Q 5 )
All intermediate terms cancel:
W = Q 0 - Q 5
Substituting Q 5 = ( 1 - η ) 5 Q 0
W = Q 0 1 - ( 1 - η ) 5
Step 3: Net efficiency
η net = W Q 0 = 1 - ( 1 - η ) 5
Given
1 - ( 1 - η ) 5 = 211 243
Therefore,
1 - η ) 5 = 1 - 211 243 = 32 243
32 243 = 2 5 3 5 = 2 3 5
Hence,
1 - η = 2 3
η = 1 3
Answer   η = 1 3 Correct option: (B) 1 3 .

For the first engine, η = W 1 Q 0 Hence heat rejected by the first engine is Q 1 = Q 0 - W 1 = Q 0 ( 1 - η ) Since Q 1 is absorbed by the second engine, Q 2 = ( 1 - η ) Q 1 = ( 1 - η ) 2 Q 0 Similarly, Q 3 = ( 1 - η ) 3 Q 0 Q 4 = ( 1 - η ) 4 Q 0 Q 5 = ( 1 - η ) 5 Q 0 Step 2: Total work done Work done by each engine: W 1 = Q 0 - Q 1 W 2 = Q 1 - Q 2 W 3 = Q 2 - Q 3 W 4 = Q 3 - Q 4 W 5 = Q 4 - Q 5 Adding all, W = W 1 + W 2 + W 3 + W 4 + W 5 W = ( Q 0 - Q 1 ) + ( Q 1 - Q 2 ) + ( Q 2 - Q 3 ) + ( Q 3 - Q 4 ) + ( Q 4 - Q 5 ) All intermediate terms cancel: W = Q 0 - Q 5 Substituting Q 5 = ( 1 - η ) 5 Q 0 W = Q 0 1 - ( 1 - η ) 5 Step 3: Net efficiency η net = W Q 0 = 1 - ( 1 - η ) 5 Given 1 - ( 1 - η ) 5 = 211 243 Therefore, 1 - η ) 5 = 1 - 211 243 = 32 243 32 243 = 2 5 3 5 = 2 3 5 Hence, 1 - η = 2 3 η = 1 3 Answer η = 1 3 Correct option: (B) 1 3 .

question_text: A Carnot engine takes in 1000 J of heat from a reservoir at 500 K and rejects heat to a sink at 250 K . Find the work done and the heat rejected.
solution_html:
Detailed Answer: Step 1: Efficiency of Carnot engine
η = 1 - T C T H
η = 1 - 250 500 = 1 - 0.5 = 0.5
So, efficiency = 50%.
Step 2: Work done
W = η ⋅ Q H = 0.5 ⋅ 1000 = 500   J
Step 3: Heat rejected
Q C = Q H - W = 1000 - 500 = 500   J
Work done = 500 J
Heat rejected = 500 J (Option a)

question_text: Two vessels, A and B, contain ideal gases in equilibrium. Vessel A contains helium ( H e ) gas at temperature T A , while vessel B contains oxygen ( O 2 ) gas at temperature T B . The average translational kinetic energy per helium molecule in vessel A is equal to three times the average rotational kinetic energy per oxygen molecule in vessel B. Assume oxygen behaves as a diatomic ideal gas with two active rotational degrees of freedom. Find the value of v r m s , H e v r m s , O 2 where v r m s , H e and v r m s , O 2 are the root-mean-square speeds of helium and oxygen molecules, respectively.
solution_html:
Detailed Answer: Step 1: Relation between kinetic energies
For helium (He) — a monatomic ideal gas:
Average translational kinetic energy per molecule = 3 2 k T A
For oxygen (O₂) — a diatomic ideal gas with two active rotational degrees of freedom:
Average rotational kinetic energy per molecule = 2 2 k T B = k T B
Given:
3 2 k T A = 3 ( k T B )
Simplify:
T A = 2 T B
Step 2: Root-mean-square (rms) speed formula
v rms = 3 k T m
So:
v rms,He v rms,O₂ = T A / m He T B / m O₂ = T A T B ⋅ m O₂ m He
Step 3: Substitute values
From Step 1: T A / T B = 2
Molar masses:
m He = 4  u
m O₂ = 32  u
v rms,He v rms,O₂ = 2 ⋅ 32 4 = 16 = 4
Final Answer:
v rms,He v rms,O₂ = 4

question_text: A Carnot engine operates between a hot reservoir at temperature T 1 and a cold reservoir at temperature T 2 . When the temperature of the cold reservoir is lowered by 62 K , the efficiency becomes 1 2 . Alternatively, when the temperature of the hot reservoir is raised by 62 K , the efficiency becomes 2 5 .Find the initial temperature of the hot reservoir T 1 -----in kelvin.
solution_html:
Detailed Answer: Step 1: Carnot efficiency formula
η = 1 - T 2 T 1
Step 2: First condition (cold reservoir lowered by 62 K). Efficiency becomes 1 2 :
1 2 = 1 - T 2 - 62 T 1
T 2 - 62 T 1 = 1 2
T 2 - 62 = T 1 2 … ( 1 )
Step 3: Second condition (hot reservoir raised by 62 K). Efficiency becomes 2 5 :
2 5 = 1 - T 2 T 1 + 62
T 2 T 1 + 62 = 3 5
T 2 = 3 5 ( T 1 + 62 ) … ( 2 )
Step 4: Solve equations (1) and (2)
From (1):
T 2 = T 1 2 + 62
From (2):
T 2 = 3 5 ( T 1 + 62 )
Equating:
T 1 2 + 62 = 3 5 ( T 1 + 62 )
Multiply through by 10:
5 T 1 + 620 = 6 T 1 + 372
620 - 372 = 6 T 1 - 5 T 1
248 = T 1
Final Answer: T 1 = 248  K

Efficiency becomes 1 2 : 1 2 = 1 - T 2 - 62 T 1 T 2 - 62 T 1 = 1 2 T 2 - 62 = T 1 2 … ( 1 ) Step 3: Second condition (hot reservoir raised by 62 K). Efficiency becomes 2 5 : 2 5 = 1 - T 2 T 1 + 62 T 2 T 1 + 62 = 3 5 T 2 = 3 5 ( T 1 + 62 ) … ( 2 ) Step 4: Solve equations (1) and (2) From (1): T 2 = T 1 2 + 62 From (2): T 2 = 3 5 ( T 1 + 62 ) Equating: T 1 2 + 62 = 3 5 ( T 1 + 62 ) Multiply through by 10: 5 T 1 + 620 = 6 T 1 + 372 620 - 372 = 6 T 1 - 5 T 1 248 = T 1 Final Answer: T 1 = 248 K

n T = constant

n f T = n 0 ⋅ 300

So final moles:

question_text: A Carnot engine operates between a source and a sink. Its initial efficiency is 1 5 . When the temperature of the sink is decreased by 80 K , the efficiency increases to 2 5 . Find the temperature of the source (in K). Answer: ______ K
solution_html:
Detailed Answer: For a Carnot engine,
η = 1 - T C T H
Initially,
1 5 = 1 - T C T H
T C = 4 5 T H
After decreasing the sink temperature by 80   K ,
2 5 = 1 - T C - 80 T H
T C - 80 T H = 3 5
Substituting T C = 4 5 T H ,
4 5 T H - 80 T H = 3 5
4 5 - 80 T H = 3 5
1 5 = 80 T H
T H = 400   K
Answer 400
(Kelvin)

question_text: The equation of parabola whose focus is (3, -4) and directrix is x-y+5=0. is
solution_html:
Detailed Answer: Let P(x, y) be any point on the parabola By definition of parabola.

SP=PM
∴ ( x - 3 ) 2 + ( y + 4 ) 2 =       | x - y + 5 1 2 + 1 2 |
On squaring both sides ,we get
( x - 3 ) 2 + ( y + 4 ) 2 =     ( x - y + 5 ) 2 ( 2 ) 2                                                  
⟹ 2 ( x 2 + y 2 - 6 x + 8 y + 25 )
= x 2 + y 2 - 2 x y + 10 x - 10 y + 25                                               
⟹ x 2 + y 2 + 2 x y - 22 x + 26 y + 25 = 0   
which is the required equation of parabola.

Axis is x - y = 0

⇒ ( x - y 2 ) 2 = 2 a ( x + y - a 2 2 )

question_text: The vertex of the parabola whose parametric equation is x = t 2 - t + 1 , y = t 2 + t + 1 , t ∈ R is
solution_html:
Detailed Answer: x = t 2 - t + 1 ,   y = t 2 + t + 1
∴ x + y = 2 t 2 + 2 and x - y = 2 t
Or 2 ( x + y - 2 ) = 4 t 2 = ( 2 t ) 2 = ( y - x ) 2
Or ( x - y ) 2 = 2 ( x + y - 2 )
⇒ ( x - y 2 ) 2 = 2 ( x + y - 2 2 )
For vertex, x - y 2 = 0 and x + y - 2 2 = 0
⇒ x = y and x + y = 2
∴ x = y = 1
Hence, vertex is (1,1).
solution_text: Detailed Answer: x = t 2 - t + 1 , y = t 2 + t + 1 ∴ x + y = 2 t 2 + 2 and x - y = 2 t Or 2 ( x + y - 2 ) = 4 t 2 = ( 2 t ) 2 = ( y - x ) 2 Or ( x - y ) 2 = 2 ( x + y - 2 ) ⇒ ( x - y 2 ) 2 = 2 ( x + y - 2 2 ) For vertex, x - y 2 = 0 and x + y - 2 2 = 0 ⇒ x = y and x + y = 2 ∴ x = y = 1 Hence, vertex is (1,1).

Detailed Answer: General equation of such parabola is y = A x 2 + B x + C

A + B + C = 6 ⋯ ( i i i )

solution_html:
Detailed Answer: Since the axis of the parabola is parallel to the X-axis, its general equation takes the form x = a y 2 + b y + c
For the point (0, 4), 0 = a ( 4 ) 2 + b ( 4 ) + c ⇒ 16 a + 4 b + c = 0 ⋯ ( i )
For (1,9), 1 = a ( 9 ) 2 + b ( 9 ) + c
⇒ 81 a + 9 b + c = 1 ⋯ ( i i )
For (-2, 6), - 2 = a ( 6 2 ) + b ( 6 ) + c
⇒ 36 a + 6 b + c = - 2 ⋯ ( i i i )
Now i i - i gives, 65 a + 5 b = 1 ⋯ 1
i i i - i gives 10 a + b = - 1 or 50 a + 5 b = - 5 ⋯ ( 2 )
( 1 ) - ( 2 ) gives a = 6 15 = 2 5
∴ b = - 5 and c = 68 5
∴ x = 2 5 y 2 - 5 y + 68 5
⇒ 5 x = 2 y 2 - 25 y + 68

question_text: A mixture contains 4 moles of helium and n moles of hydrogen. The rms speed of the gas molecules in the mixture is 2 times the speed of sound in the mixture. The value of n is:
solution_html:
Detailed Answer: For an ideal gas mixture, v r m s = 3 R T M
and the speed of sound is v s = γ R T M
where M is the mean molar mass of the mixture and γ is the ratio of specific heats.
Given, v r m s = 2   v s
Squaring both sides,
3 R T M = 2 γ R T M
3 = 2 γ
γ = 3 2
For the mixture:
Helium (monatomic):
C V , He = 3 R 2
Hydrogen (diatomic): C V , H 2 = 5 R 2
Total heat capacity at constant volume:
C V = 4 ( 3 R 2 ) + n ( 5 R 2 ) = R 2 ( 12 + 5 n )
Total heat capacity at constant pressure:
C P = C V + ( 4 + n ) R = R 2 ( 20 + 7 n )
Therefore, γ = C P C V = 20 + 7 n 12 + 5 n
Since γ = 3 2 ,
20 + 7 n 12 + 5 n = 3 2
2 ( 20 + 7 n ) = 3 ( 12 + 5 n )
40 + 14 n = 36 + 15 n
n = 4
Answer: n = 4
Correct Option: (b) 4.

α + 5 α = 33 28 .
Cross-multiplying,
28 ( α + 5 ) = 33 α
28 α + 140 = 33 α
5 α = 140
α = 28 .  
Answer α = 28
Correct Option: (c) 28.

question_text: How much heat energy should be supplied to a gaseous mixture consisting of 1 g of hydrogen (H₂) and 1 g of helium (He) to raise its temperature from 0°C to 100°C: (a) at constant volume and (b) at constant pressure Given: R = 2 cal mol - 1 K - 1 The values of heat supplied ( Q V Q P ) are:
solution_html:
Detailed Answer: Given: Mass of hydrogen, m H 2 = 1 g,
Mass of helium, m H e = 1 g.
Temperature rise, Δ T = 100 ∘ C = 100  K
R = 2   cal mol - 1 K - 1
For hydrogen: n H 2 = 1 2 = 0.5  mol
For helium: n H e = 1 4 = 0.25  mol
For hydrogen (diatomic gas), C V = 5 R 2
For helium (monoatomic gas), C V = 3 R 2
Hence,
Q V = n H 2 5 R 2 Δ T + n H e 3 R 2 Δ T
= 0.5 × 5 × 2 2 × 100 + 0.25 × 3 × 2 2 × 100
= 250 + 75
Q V = 325  cal
For hydrogen, C P = 7 R 2
For helium, C P = 5 R 2
Therefore,
Q P = n H 2 7 R 2 Δ T + n H e 5 R 2 Δ T
= 0.5 × 7 × 2 2 × 100 + 0.25 × 5 × 2 2 × 100
= 350 + 125
Q P = 475  cal
Q V = 325  cal , Q P = 475  cal
Correct Option: A) 325 cal, 475 cal

Mass of each molecule is doubled

Speed of each molecule is halved ⇒ v ’ 2 = ( v 2 ) 2 = v 2 4
Therefore,
P ’ = 1 3 ( 2 ρ ) ( v 2 4 )
P ’ = 1 2 ( 1 3 ρ v 2 )
P ’ = P 0 2
Answer: P = P 0 2

K Ar K H 2 = 3 2 k T 3 2 k T = 1   .
K Ar K H 2 = 1

question_text: An ideal monoatomic gas undergoes a polytropic process governed by the relation P V 3 = constant . During this process, 2.0 moles of the gas cool down by exactly 60 K . If the magnitude of the total heat exchanged by the gas during the process can be written as k R , where R is the universal gas constant, determine the value of k .
solution_html:
Detailed Answer: For a polytropic process, P V n = constant with n = 3 .
Given: N = 2 , Δ T = - 60  K and the gas is monoatomic
so C V = 3 2 R .
Step 1: Change in internal energy
Δ U = N C V Δ T
Δ U = 2 3 2 R ( - 60 ) = - 180 R .
Step 2: Work done
For a polytropic process
W = N R Δ T 1 - n .
Substituting n = 3 , W = 2 R ( - 60 ) 1 - 3 = - 120 R - 2 = 60 R .
Step 3: Heat exchanged
Using the first law of thermodynamics,
Q = Δ U + W .
Q = - 180 R + 60 R = - 120 R .
Therefore, the magnitude of heat exchanged is
∣ Q ∣ = 120 R .
Comparing with
∣ Q ∣ = k R ,
we get k = 120 . Answer: 120

question_text: A rigid, thermally insulated closed container is split into two chambers by a locked, non-conducting piston. Chamber 1 contains 2.0 moles of an ideal monoatomic gas at a temperature of 300 K . Chamber 2 contains 3.0 moles of an ideal rigid diatomic gas at a temperature of 450 K . The partition is unlocked and replaced with a perfectly heat-conducting, frictionless thin piston, allowing both chambers to eventually reach thermal and mechanical equilibrium without any heat escaping the outer container. If the final equilibrium temperature is T f , find the value of ( T f 350 ) in Kelvin.
solution_html:
Detailed Answer: Since the outer container is thermally insulated, the total internal energy of the system remains constant.
For an ideal gas, U = n C V T . Monoatomic gas
C V 1 = 3 2 R
U 1 = 2 3 2 R ( 300 ) = 900 R .
Rigid diatomic gas
For a rigid diatomic gas,
C V 2 = 5 2 R .
U 2 = 3 5 2 R ( 450 ) = 3375 R .
Total initial energy: U i = 900 R + 3375 R = 4275 R . At equilibrium, both gases have the same temperature T f .
Thus,
U f = 2 3 2 R T f + 3 5 2 R T f .
U f = ( 3 R + 7.5 R ) T f = 10.5 R T f .   
Conservation of energy:
10.5 R T f = 4275 R .   
T f = 4275 10.5 = 407.14  K . Required quantity
T f - 350 = 407.14 - 350 = 57.14  K .  
57.1  K
Answer: 57  K

Monoatomic gas C V 1 = 3 2 R U 1 = 2 3 2 R ( 300 ) = 900 R . Rigid diatomic gas For a rigid diatomic gas, C V 2 = 5 2 R . U 2 = 3 5 2 R ( 450 ) = 3375 R . Total initial energy: U i = 900 R + 3375 R = 4275 R . At equilibrium, both gases have the same temperature T f . Thus, U f = 2 3 2 R T f + 3 5 2 R T f . U f = ( 3 R + 7.5 R ) T f = 10.5 R T f . Conservation of energy: 10.5 R T f = 4275 R . T f = 4275 10.5 = 407.14 K . Required quantity T f - 350 = 407.14 - 350 = 57.14 K . 57.1 K Answer: 57 K

question_text: Two identical vessels are connected by a thin tube and contain the same ideal gas. Initially, P 1 = P 2 = P , T 1 = T , T 2 = 3 T . The valve is opened and equilibrium is established. Let R be the ratio of the final molecular collision rate on the walls of vessel 1 to its initial value. Find the value of 150 R 2 .
solution_html:
Detailed Answer: Let the volume of each vessel be V .
Initially, P 1 = P 2 = P , T 1 = T , T 2 = 3 T .
Initial number of moles
For vessel 1, n 1 = P V R T .
For vessel 2, n 2 = P V R ( 3 T ) = P V 3 R T .
Hence, n total = 4 P V 3 R T .
Final equilibrium temperature
Since the system is thermally insulated externally and the gas is the same in both vessels,
T f = n 1 T 1 + n 2 T 2 n 1 + n 2 .
Substituting,
T f = P V R T T + P V 3 R T ( 3 T ) P V R T + P V 3 R T = 2 P V / R 4 P V / ( 3 R T ) = 3 T 2 .
Thus,
T f = 3 T 2 .
Final pressure: P f ( 2 V ) = n total R T f .
Substituting, P f ( 2 V ) = ( 4 P V 3 R T R 3 T 2 ) = 2 P V .
Hence, P f = P .
Collision rate
The molecular collision rate on the walls is proportional to
Z ∝ n v ˉ where n = P k B T , v ˉ ∝ T .
Therefore, Z ∝ P T . So, R = Z f Z i = P f / T f P / T = T T f .
Since P f = P , R = T 3 T / 2 = 2 3 .
Hence, R 2 = 2 3 .
Required quantity
150 R 2 = 150 ( 2 3 ) = 100 .
100

∴ equation of tangent passing through (1, 7) and having slope 2 is y - 7 = 2 ( x - 1 ) ⇒ 2 x - y + 5 = 0
Given equation of circle is x 2 + y 2 + 16 x + 12 y + c = 0
⇒ g = 8 ,   g = 6 ⇒ centre = (-8, -6)
Now, distance of centre (-8, -6) from the tangent 2 x - y + 5 = 0 is | 2 ( - 8 ) + ( - 1 ) ( - 6 ) + 5 | 4 + 1 = 5
If the tangent touches the circle, then distance of tangent from centre = radius
⇒ 5 = g 2 + f 2 - c ⇒ 5 = 100 - c ⇒ c = 95

question_text: If the coordinates of the point on the parabola y = x 2 = 7 x + 2 which is nearest to the straight line y = 3 x - 3 is ( k 1 , k 2 ) , then the value of | k 1 + k 2 | is
solution_html:
Detailed Answer: y = x 2 = 7 x + 2 ⇒ ( x + 7 2 ) 2 = y + 41 4
Now, tangent parallel to y = 3 x - 3 will have slope m = 3 and its point of contact will be x + 7 2 = 2 a m ⇒ x + 7 2 = 2 × 1 4 × 3 ⇒ x = - 2
And y + 41 4 = a m 2 ⇒ y + 41 4 = 1 4 × 9 ⇒ y = - 8
Hence, nearest point on the parabola from the line y = 3 x - 3 is ( - 2 ,   - 8 )
k 1 = - 2 ,   k 2 = - 8 ⇒ | k 1 + k 2 | = 10

(take g=10ms-2)
question_text: The mass of a lift is 500 kg. What will be the tension in its cable when it is going up with an acceleration of 2ms -2 (take g=10ms -2 )
solution_html:
Detailed Answer: Let the tension in the cable be T
The equation of motion for the lift is:
T - m g = m a  where m = mass of the lift, a =  acceleration of the lift
T = m ( g + a )
⇒ T = 500 × 12 = 6000 N
solution_text: Detailed Answer: Let the tension in the cable be T The equation of motion for the lift is: T - m g = m a where m = mass of the lift, a = acceleration of the lift T = m ( g + a ) ⇒ T = 500 × 12 = 6000 N

⇒ 1 tan ⁡ θ 1 - 1 tan ⁡ θ = sin ⁡ θ   + cos ⁡ θ ⇒ 1 tan ⁡ θ - 1 = sin ⁡ θ + cos ⁡ θ ⇒ cos ⁡ θ sin ⁡ θ - cos ⁡ θ = sin ⁡ θ + cos ⁡ θ
⇒ cos ⁡ θ = sin 2 ⁡ θ - cos 2 ⁡ θ = 1 - 2 cos 2 ⁡ θ ⇒ 2 cos 2 ⁡ θ + cos ⁡ θ - 1 = 0 ⇒ ( 2 cos ⁡ θ - 1 ) ( cos ⁡ θ + 1 ) = 0
⇒ cos ⁡ θ = 1 2 or cos ⁡ θ = - 1   (rejected) ⇒ θ = π 3 ⇒ tan ⁡ θ = 3

Detailed Answer: f ( x ) = 4 x 4 x + 2 , ⇒ f ( 1 - x ) = 4 1 - x 4 1 - x + 2 = 2 2 + 4 x ⇒ f ( x ) + f ( 1 - x ) = 1
Let S = f ( 1 20 ) + f ( 2 20 ) + … + f ( 19 20 ) ⇒ S = f ( 19 20 ) + f ( 18 20 ) + … + f ( 1 20 )

question_text: If the roots of x 2 + 2 a x + b = 0 are real and they differ by almost 2 m , then b lies in the interval
solution_html:
Detailed Answer: Let the roots are α and β
∴ α + β = - 2 a and α β = b
Also given that | α - β | ≤ 2 m  
  ⇒ ( α - β ) 2 ≤ 4 m 2
Now, ( α + β ) 2 - 4 α β = ( α - β ) 2   
⇒ 4 a 2 - 4 b ≤ 4 m 2 ⇒ a 2 - b ≤ m 2
⇒ a 2 - m 2 ≤ b # ( i )
Also, the discriminant 4 a 2 - 4 b ≥ 0 (as roots are real)
⇒ a 2 ≥ b # ( i i )
From (i) and (ii), we have
a 2 - m 2 ≤ b ≤ a 2
i.e.,  b ∈ [ a 2 - m 2 , a 2 ]

question_text: The difference between the greatest and least values of the function f ( x ) = c o s ⁡ x + ( 1 2 ) c o s ⁡ 2 x - ( 1 3 ) c o s ⁡ 3 x is
solution_html:
Detailed Answer: The given function is periodic, with period 2 π . So the difference between the greatest and least values of the function is the difference between these values on the interval [ 0,2 π ] . We have
f ' ( x ) = - ( s i n ⁡ x + s i n ⁡ 2 x - s i n ⁡ 3 x )
= - 4 s i n ⁡ x s i n ⁡ ( 3 x 2 ) s i n ⁡ ( x 2 )
Hence x = 0 , 2 π 3 , π and 2 π are the critical points.Also, f ( 0 ) = 1 + 1 2 - 1 3 = 7 6 , f ( 2 π 3 ) = - 13 12 ,
f ( π ) = - 1 6  and  f ( 2 π ) = 7 6
Hence the greatest value is 7 6 and the least value is ( - 13 12 ) . Hence the difference is 7 6 - ( - 13 12 ) = 27 12 = 9 4

question_text: If l o g ⁡ 2 ( x 2 - p x + q ) = l o g ⁡ 2 ( x + 1 ) has exactly two distinct real solutions, both of which are roots of x 2 - 4 x + 2 = 0 , then
solution_html:
Detailed Answer: Given l o g ⁡ 2 ( x 2 - p x + q ) = l o g ⁡ 2 ( x + 1 ) .
Since the bases are the same and 2 > 1 , x 2 - p x + q = x + 1 ,
with domain conditions x + 1 > 0 , x 2 - p x + q > 0 .
Thus the equation reduces to
x 2 - ( p + 1 ) x + ( q - 1 ) = 0 .
We are told that it has exactly two distinct real solutions, and both are roots of x 2 - 4 x + 2 = 0 .
Since x 2 - 4 x + 2 = 0 has two distinct roots, the quadratic
x 2 - ( p + 1 ) x + ( q - 1 ) = 0 must have exactly the same roots. Therefore,
x 2 - ( p + 1 ) x + ( q - 1 ) ≡ x 2 - 4 x + 2 .
Comparing coefficients,
p + 1 = 4 ⇒ p = 3 , q - 1 = 2 ⇒ q = 3 .
So the only possible pair is ( p , q ) = ( 3,3 ) .   
Check domain:
Roots of x 2 - 4 x + 2 = 0 are x = 2 ± 2 ,
both satisfy x + 1 > 0 . Hence both are valid logarithmic solutions.
But 3 3 is not among the options.

question_text: Eight distinct students are to be seated around a circular table. Among them are three friends A , B , C .How many circular arrangements are possible such that No two of A , B , C sit adjacent, and A is not opposite B ?
solution_html:
Detailed Answer: Total circular arrangements
= ( 8 - 1 ) ! = 7 ! = 5040 .
We count arrangements where A , B , C are pairwise non-adjacent.
Fix A .
Arrange the remaining five non-special students:
5 ! = 120 .
These five create five internal gaps and one wrap-around gap, giving 6 gaps.
Since A occupies one position, effectively there are 5 allowable gaps for placing B and C so that they are not adjacent to A or each other.
Choose two gaps: ( 5 2 ) = 10 .
Arrange B , C : 2 ! .
Hence 120 × 10 × 2 = 2400 .
Now subtract those with A opposite B .
Once A is fixed, B has exactly one opposite seat.
Repeating the gap argument gives 1920 .
Therefore 2400 - 1920 = 480

The experiment is repeated, and all conditions remain the same with the exception that the horizontal force is doubled. What happens to the box's acceleration? It increases to more than double its original value.

options.html: 1 ) It increases to more than double its original value.
options.text: 1 ) It increases to more than double its original value.

options.html: 2 ) It increases to exactly double its original value.
options.text: 2 ) It increases to exactly double its original value.

options.html: 3 ) It increases to less than double its original value.
options.text: 3 ) It increases to less than double its original value.

solution_html:
Detailed Answer: As the box is sliding, kinetic friction ( f k ) tries to decelerate the object while the external force (call it F) is accelerating it (Note that to make the box slide, F > f k ). If a 1 is the acceleration of the box in the first case, Newton’s II Law gives:
F - f k = m a 1 ⟹ a 1 = F - f k m
Here, as the vertical force is not changing, f k = μ m g is constant.
If the horizontal forces now doubled, the new acceleration is:
a 2 = 2 F - f k m
⟹ a 2 a 1 = 2 F - f k F - f k = 1 + F F - f k   
Since F > F - f k ,     F F - f k > 1
⟹ 1 + F F - f k > 2 ⟹ a 2 a 1 > 2 ⟹ a 2 > 2 a 1

Because of their gravitational attraction, they head toward each other on a collision course. When their center-to-center separation is d, the speed of planet of mass 2M is:
solution_html:
Detailed Answer: As there is no external force on the system, linear momentum of the system is conserved.
Let v 1 and v 2 be the speeds of the spheres of mass M and 2M respectively
Conservation of linear momentum gives
M v 1 - 2 M v 2 = 0 ⟹ v 1 = 2 v 2
Conservation of mechanical energy gives
1 2 M v 1 2 + 1 2 ( 2 M ) v 2 2 - G M 2 M d = 0
⟹   1 2 4 v 2 2 + v 2 2 = 2 G M d
⟹ v 2 = 2 G M 3 d

question_text: A wire, which passes through the hole in a small bead, is bent in the form of a quarter of a circle. The wire is fixed vertically on ground as shown in the figure. The bead is released from near the top of the wire and it slides along the wire without friction. As the bead moves from A to B, the force it applies on the wire is:

options.html: 3 ) radially outwards initially and radially inwards later.
options.text: 3 ) radially outwards initially and radially inwards later.

options.html: 4 ) radially inwards initially and radially outwards later.
options.text: 4 ) radially inwards initially and radially outwards later.

solution_html:
Detailed Answer: Let v be speed of the bead when it makes an angle θ with the vertical direction. N is the force on the bead by the wire.

By conservation of energy,
1 2 m v 2 = m g r ( 1 - cos ⁡ θ ) ⟹ m v 2 = 2 m g r ( 1 - cos ⁡ θ )
Using II Law for radial direction,
m g cos ⁡ θ - N = m v 2 r ⟹ m v 2 = r m g cos ⁡ θ - N
Eliminating m v 2 from the equations, we get:
2 m g r 1 - cos ⁡ θ = r ( m g cos ⁡ θ - N )
⟹ N   = m g ( 3 cos ⁡ θ - 2 )
We see that, for cos ⁡ θ < 2 / 3 , N is directed along radial outward direction. After cos ⁡ θ > 2 / 3 , N becomes negative which implies that the normal force points in radial inward direction. Therefore, the force on the wire due to the bead is radially inward initially and radially outward later (By III law).

question_text: The displacement x (in metre) of a particle in simple harmonic motion is related to time t (in second) as x = 0.01 cos ⁡ ( π t + π 4 ) The frequency of the motion will be
solution_html:
Detailed Answer: The standard equation in SHM is
               x = a cos ⁡ ( ω t + ∅ )                    …(i)
Where a is amplitude, ω the angular velocity and ( ∅ ) the phase difference.
Also,     ω = 2 π T     w h e r e   T is periodic time.
So, Eq. (i) becomes
             x = a cos ⁡ ( 2 π t T + ∅ )               …(ii)
Given, equation is
  x = 0.01 cos ⁡ ( 2 π t 2 + π 4 )                 …(iii)
Comparing Eq. (ii) with Eq. (iii), we get
            2 π t T = 2 π t 2
⇒                   T = 2 s
So, frequency n = 1 T = 1 2 = 0.5 Hz

[ C ] = T - 1
Base of the exponent:
Since θ represents the base of the exponent, it is a dimensionless quantity ( [ θ ] = 1 ), meaning the entire term θ - 2 C t is dimensionless:
[ θ - 2 C t ] = 1
Combining these, the dimension of the RHS is:
[ R H S ] = [ B ] [ C ] = [ B ] T - 1

L - 1 / 2   T 1 / 2 = [ B ] T - 1

[ B ] = L - 1 / 2   T 1 / 2 ⋅   T 1 = L - 1 / 2   T 3 / 2

⇒ O n   b a l a n c i n g   c h a r g e ,

100 g of propane = 1 44 × 100 = 2.27   m o l
32 g of O 2 = 1 mole of O 2

Moles of C O 2 formed = 3 × 2.7 = 6.681   m o l   o f   C O 2
When reaction is completed 19.90 moles of O 2 , 6.81 moles of C O 2 and 9.08 moles of steam are left in the flask.
Mole fraction of C O 2 = M o l e s   o f   C O 2 g T o t a l   n u m b e r   o f   m o l e s   = 6.81 19.90 + 6.81 + 9.08 = 0.19
x × 10 - 2 = 19 × 10 - 2

Detailed Answer: The east and north components of the displacement from Dallas (D) to Chicago (C) are the sums of the east and north components of the displacements from Dallas to Atlanta (A) and from Atlanta to Chicago. In equation form:
d DC east    = d DA east  + d AC east    = ( 730 m i ) c o s ⁡ 5.00 ∘ - ( 560 m i ) s i n ⁡ 21.0 ∘ = 527  miles  d DC north    = d DA north  + d AC north    = ( 730 m i ) s i n ⁡ 5.00 ∘ + ( 560 m i ) c o s ⁡ 21.0 ∘ = 586  miles 
By the Pythagorean theorem,
d = d D C  east  2 + d D C  north  2 = 788 m i
Then,   θ = t a n - 1 ⁡ d D C  north  d D C  east  = 48.0 ∘
Thus, Chicago is 788 miles at 48.0 ∘ northeast of Dallas.

question_text: Your dog is running around the grass in your back yard. He undergoes successive displacements 3.50 m south, 8.20 m northeast, and 15.0 m west. What is the resultant displacement?
solution_html:
Detailed Answer: We use the unit-vector addition method. It is just as easy to add three displacements as to add two.
We take the direction east to be along + i ˆ .
The three displacements can be written as:
d → 1   = ( - 3.50   m ) j ˆ d → 2   = ( 8.20   m ) c o s ⁡ 45.0 ∘ i ˆ + ( 8.20   m ) s i n ⁡ 45.0 ∘ j ˆ   = ( 5.80   m ) i ˆ + ( 5.80   m ) j ˆ d → 3   = ( - 15.0   m ) i ˆ
The resultant is
R →   = d → 1 + d → 2 + d → 3 = ( - 15.0   m + 5.80   m ) i ˆ + ( 5.80   m - 3.50   m ) j ˆ   = ( - 9.20   m ) i ˆ + ( 2.30   m ) j ˆ
(or 9.20 m west and 2.30 m north).
The magnitude of the resultant displacement is
| R → | = R x 2 + R y 2 = ( - 9.20 m ) 2 + ( 2.30 m ) 2 = 9.48   m

question_html: A snow-covered ski slope makes an angle of 35.0 ∘ with the horizontal. When a ski jumper plummets onto the hill, a parcel of splashed snow is thrown up to a maximum displacement of 1.50 m at 16.0 ∘ from the vertical in the uphill direction as shown in Figure P3.28. Find the components of its maximum displacement , perpendicular to the surface.(cos 41 = 0.6293)
question_text: A snow-covered ski slope makes an angle of 35.0 ∘ with the horizontal. When a ski jumper plummets onto the hill, a parcel of splashed snow is thrown up to a maximum displacement of 1.50 m at 16.0 ∘ from the vertical in the uphill direction as shown in Figure P3.28. Find the components of its maximum displacement , perpendicular to the surface.(cos 41 = 0.6293)
solution_html:
Detailed Answer: We take the x axis along the slope downhill. (Students, get used to this choice!)
The y axis is perpendicular to the slope, at 35.0 ∘ to the vertical.
Then the displacement of the snow makes an angle of 90.0 ∘ + 35.0 ∘ + 16.0 ∘ = 141 ∘ with the x axis.

(a) Its component parallel to the surface is ( 1.50   m ) c o s ⁡ 141 ∘ = - 1.17   m , or 1.17 m toward the top of the hill.
(b) Its component perpendicular to the surface is ( 1.50   m ) s i n ⁡ 141 ∘ = 0.944   m , or 0.944 m away from the snow.

2 x 2 + ( a + b ) x + 27 = 0

⇒   a = - 7  and  b = - 8
∴   | a + b | = | - 7 - 8 | = | - 15 | = 15
Thus, | a + b | 2 = 15 2 = 7.5

We need to solve the inequalities a 2 - a 4 + 8 2 < x 1 < a 2 + a 4 + 8 2 .
After solving these inequalities for various positive integral values of a ,
we find that the smallest positive integral value of a that satisfies both inequalities is a = 3 .

question_text: A particle crossing the origin of coordinates at  time t = 0, moves in the x-y plane with a constant acceleration ‘a’ in the y direction. If its equation of motion  is y = bx 2 (b is a constant), its velocity component in  the x direction is :
solution_html:
Detailed Answer:
Differentiate y = bx2 w.r.t. time to get the velocity  component in y direction
d y d t = 2 b x d x d t
Differentiate once again to get the acceleration component in y direction
d 2 y d t 2 = 2 b x d 2 x d t 2 + 2 b ( d x d t ) 2
The particle moves with a constant acceleration along y direction. Thus,
d 2 y d t 2 = a and d 2 x d t 2 = 0
⟹ d 2 y d t 2 = a = 2 b ( v x ) 2
⟹ v x = a 2 b
Note that x component of velocity is constant (as expected).
solution_text: Detailed Answer: Differentiate y = bx 2 w.r.t. time to get the velocity  component in y direction d y d t = 2 b x d x d t Differentiate once again to get the acceleration component in y direction d 2 y d t 2 = 2 b x d 2 x d t 2 + 2 b ( d x d t ) 2 The particle moves with a constant acceleration along y direction. Thus, d 2 y d t 2 = a and d 2 x d t 2 = 0 ⟹ d 2 y d t 2 = a = 2 b ( v x ) 2 ⟹ v x = a 2 b Note that x component of velocity is constant (as expected).

solution_html:
Detailed Answer: The x coordinate of the particle at time t is:
x = v 0 x t + 1 2 a x t 2 = 3 t - t 2 2
When the particle reaches maximum x coordinate,
d x d t = v x = 0 ⟹ 3 - t = 0 ⟹ t = 3   s
The y coordinate of the particle at t is:
y = v 0 y t + 1 2 a y t 2 = - t 2 4
v y = d y d t = - t 2 = - 1.5   m s - 1   at t = 3 s
Hence, the speed of the particle at t = 3 s is 1.5 m/s

question_html: Which of the following statements is correct about Bohr’s stationary orbits?
question_text: Which of the following statements is correct about Bohr’s stationary orbits?

options.html: 3 ) energy of the electron remains constant
options.text: 3 ) energy of the electron remains constant

options.html: 4 ) angular momentum of the electron is <math> <mfrac> <mrow> <mi>h</mi> </mrow> <mrow> <mn>2</mn> <mi>π</mi> </mrow> </mfrac> </math>
options.text: 4 ) angular momentum of the electron is h 2 π

solution_html:
Detailed Answer: According to Niels Bohr's atomic theory, electrons revolve around the nucleus in certain specific, non-radiating circular paths known as stationary orbits or discrete energy levels. The term "stationary" does not mean the electrons themselves are at rest; rather, it indicates that the total mechanical energy of the electron stays constant as long as it continuously moves within that particular orbit. Energy is only absorbed or emitted when an electron jumps from one energy level to another.
Bohr's quantization condition states that the angular momentum (L) must be an integral multiple of h 2 π , where n = 1 ,   2 ,   3 ,   4 … . . The value is exactly h 2 π only for the first ground-state orbit ( n = 1 ) , but not for the stationary orbits in general.

Energy is only absorbed or emitted when an electron jumps from one energy level to another. Bohr's quantization condition states that the angular momentum (L) must be an integral multiple of h 2 π , where n = 1 , 2 , 3 , 4 … . . The value is exactly h 2 π only for the first ground-state orbit ( n = 1 ) , but not for the stationary orbits in general.

solution_html:
Detailed Answer: Since, total number of possible subsets of a set A and B are 2 m and 2 n ,respectively.
According to the given condition , 2 m - 2 n =56
2 m - 2 n =64-8
2 m - 2 n = 2 6 - 2 3
=>m=6 and n=3

Thus, initial height of the second ball is y = H + h = 1.25 + 1.25 = 2.5 m.

question_text: A disc of radius 1 m rotates about a fixed axis passing through its centre (axis is perpendicular to the plane of the disc). Its rotation angle varies as θ = 2 t 2 , where t is in second and θ is in radian. The magnitude  of acceleration of a point on its periphery at time t = 1 s is :
solution_html:
Detailed Answer: Angular velocity of the point is:
ω = d θ d t = 2 2 t
The linear velocity of the point is:
v = r ω = 2 2 r t ⟹ a t = d v d t = 2 2 r
The radial acceleration (centripetal acceleration) of the point is given by
a c = v 2 r = 8 r t 2
The magnitude of the acceleration of the point is
a = a t 2 + a c 2 = 8 r 2 + 64 r 2 t 4

solution_html:
Detailed Answer: The time taken by the cart to cover a distance d = 60 m is t = d/v = 60/30 = 2 s.

question_text: A body falling freely from a given height H hits an inclined plane in its path at a height h. As a result of this impact the direction of the velocity of the body becomes horizontal. The body will take maximum time to reach the ground if H h = ………..
solution_html:
Detailed Answer: Let the body is released from A, it strikes the inclined plane at B and finally reaches the ground at C.

The time taken by the body to travel from A to B is given by
t A B = 2 g ( H - h ) g
The direction of velocity of the body becomes horizontal after striking at B.
Thus, the time taken by the body to travel from B to C is t B C = 2 h g
Thus, the total time taken by the body to reach the ground is
t = 2 g ( H - h ) g + 2 h g
The value of h for maximizing t is given by dt/dh = 0
⟹ H h = 2

question_text: Which electronic level would allow the hydrogen atom to absorb a photon but not to emit it?
solution_html: Detailed Answer: The 1 s electronic level represents the ground state of a hydrogen atom ( n = 1 ) , which is its lowest possible energy state. question_text: The number of correct statements from the following is ___. A. For 1 s orbital, the probability density is maximum at the nucleus B. solution_html:
Detailed Answer: For a 2 s orbital, the probability density is maximum at the nucleus, then decreases to zero (this is the radial node), and then rises again to a secondary peak before gradually tapering off.
The boundary surface usually encloses a region where there is approximately a 90% chance of finding the electron, not 100%.

Hence, 4 elements are needed to make R 2 symmetric. ∴ N = 4 .
